user.title: Move Sensor BLE OTA
user.description: BLE OTA for the motion sensor via Bluetooth proxies. Leave the key empty to read move_sensor_ble_ota_key from /config/esphome/secrets.yaml.

data_description.ota_password: For flashing over Wi-Fi in service mode (sensor firmware 1.4.0+). Stored in /config/esphome/secrets.yaml (move_sensor_ota_password). Empty — keep the current one, or generate a random one and save it if there is none. To view or change: ESPHome Builder → Secrets.
data_description.api_key: 32 bytes, base64. Encrypts the sensor–HA link in service mode; the integration puts it into the sensor's ESPHome device itself — no confirmation after flashing. Stored in secrets.yaml (move_sensor_api_key). Empty — keep the current one, or generate and save one if there is none.

error.bad_api_key: The API key is 32 bytes in base64 (44 characters ending with «=»). Leave it empty and the integration generates one.

upload.title: Upload firmware
upload.description: Pick a .bin built by ESPHome (OTA format or factory). It is checked, saved to the firmware folder and — if enabled — flashed at the next sensor wake (PIR or telemetry).

data_description.keep_images: Older .bin files in the firmware folder are deleted after every build and upload. The image being flashed or waiting for a window is never deleted.

Stored in secrets.yaml (move_sensor_api_key). Empty — keep the current one, or generate and save one if there is none.

auth_failed.title: {name}: OTA key rejected by the sensor
auth_failed.description:
The sensor rejected the BLE OTA key, so firmware updates, settings and diagnostics are paused for it (BLE connections stopped to save its battery). Sensor data via BTHome still works.

The key in Home Assistant comes from the integration options («OTA key»); if that field is empty, from `{secret}` in `{path}`. The sensor has the key that was in secrets.yaml when its firmware was built.

Fix: make the keys match — set the right key in the options (or `{secret}`), or rebuild and flash the sensor over USB with the current secrets.yaml. Connections resume by themselves when the key changes, after Read settings / a flash, or every {hours} h.

no_key.title: {name}: no OTA key
no_key.description:
There is no BLE OTA key: the «OTA key» field in the integration options is empty and `{secret}` was not found in `{path}`. Firmware updates, settings and diagnostics over BLE are paused. Sensor data via BTHome still works.

Fix: add `{secret}` to `{path}` (the same value the firmware was built with) or enter the key in the options.

battery_low.title: {name}: battery is low ({pct} %)
battery_low.description:
The battery of **{name}** is at {pct} %, at or below the warning level you set ({level} %). About {days} days left at the current rate.

Charge the battery. This notice goes away by itself once the battery is back above {level} % + 5 %.

The warning level is the «Battery low level» setting of the sensor.

battery_empty.title: {name}: sensor stopped, battery empty
battery_empty.description:
**{name}** has not reported since {last}. Its last battery voltage was {volt} V, so it most likely ran out of power.

Charge the battery. The sensor starts reporting again on its own and this notice goes away.

not_reporting.title: {name}: sensor not reporting
not_reporting.description:
**{name}** has not reported since {last}, while its battery was fine ({pct} %).

Check that the sensor is within range of a Bluetooth adapter or Bluetooth proxy, and that it is not switched off. This notice goes away once the sensor reports again.

pir_stuck.title: {name}: motion stuck on «detected»
pir_stuck.description:
**{name}** has reported motion without a break for more than {minutes} minutes. The motion sensor may be stuck, or something keeps moving in front of it (a curtain, a heater, a pet).

This notice goes away once the sensor reports «clear» again. The time limit is the «PIR stuck after» setting.
